title: Billy Taylor as a high school pianist in 1936
summary: Phillips met Billy Taylor in 1936 at Dunbar High School, where his mother sometimes would not let him play gigs; young pianists copied Earl Hines and Teddy Wilson.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: That's interesting. How about Billy Taylor -- pianist Billy Taylor. The guy who came from North Carolina. Do you remember him?
That played here, in town?
Yeah. He would have come here... He became real famous. Dr. Billy Taylor.
He lives here. This is his home.
Yeah. Do you know him?
Sure. He used to play with us.
When did you first run into him?

In about 1936-37. He was going to Dunbar High School. He'd play with us some nights and his mother wouldn't let him go to... He'd play at nights, and she'd say "He can't go." We'd come by to pick him up. "He can't go tonight." We'd say, "We ain't got no piano player." "I can't help that." I was tellin' him about that... You know, he's been down to Charlie's, Billy has.
You're talking about Charlie's in Georgetown, where you work now.
Yeah, where I work. Well, he's been down there... So she came down there too. You know, he's a big man
Phillips - 179
now. She came down there. He almost had them packed in there like this chick, Nancy...
Nancy Wilson.
Because he's a home boy. His old man was a prominent doctor here in town, his grandfather was a big preacher. He got a big name to start with.
He's from North Carolina, though, isn't he?
No. He went to school...
I thought he came up here when he was really young or something.
Maybe he did. He could have. I know when I met him, he was a young boy going to school here.
What year did you first meet him?
What kind of playing was he doing in 1936?
He was playing good. Everybody was trying to play like Earl Hines, you know, and Teddy Wilson. Teddy was John's idol. John sounds like Teddy now when he plays. He plays a lot of things like Teddy.
So Billy Taylor, Dude Brown, John Malachi, Frank Wess...
Yeah.
